title: Proposal of Photoionization and Photofield Tunneling of Electrons as (Indirect) Evaporation Mechanisms during Laser-assisted Field Evaporation of Insulators
content: Atom probe tomography is a materials analysis technique that can attain highly localized chemical information with high sensitivity for all elements. It is based on field evaporation of ions in a high electrostatic field. To achieve this, a needle shaped specimen with an apex radius smaller than 100 nm is exposed to high voltages thereby creating electrostatic fields in the range of tens of V/nm. The sample is held at cryogenic temperatures during the experiment. For conducting materials an additional voltage pulse is used to ionize surface atoms towards a position-sensitive detector by time-of-flight mass spectrometry. The ion species is identified by time-of-flight mass spectrometry and an algorithm allows for the reconstruction of the evaporated volume. [1,2]
